THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.4,40,444/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.

3. The Tribunal has held that the claimant also contributed to an extent of 5% to the accident and this is on the premise that the claimant's breath smelt of alcohol at the time of the hospitalization.
Since the claimant was a pedestrian, the question of attributing negligence on him on the basis that he was under the influence of alcohol is unjustified.
The apportionment of the contributory negligence at 5% on the claimant is therefore set aside and it is held that the driver of the lorry himself was responsible for the accident.

4. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries:
Cut lacerated wound of 1 cm. on the forehead left side, degloving of left foot exposing bones.
5. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation:
 Sl. Compensation under Amount  No. different Heads in (Rs.)
1 . Pain and agony 75,000
2. Loss of future income 3,02,400  3.

sentences.text: ( Less) 5% contributory negligence 23,181 on the part of the claimant
The Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered disability to the extent of 20% to the whole body.
The evidence on record indicates that the doctor has opined that the claimant had suffered disability at 22.5% to whole body.

The evidence on record also indicates that the claimant has suffered amputation to mid foot and since the claimant is a labourer, the absence of a part of the foot would result in serious functional disability to his work and therefore, I am of the view that it would be appropriate to determine the functional disability at 25%.
7. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.9,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2018, would be Rs.12,500/-.

8. Since the claimant has suffered disability at 25% and was aged 39 years as per the Audhar Card which was marked at Ex.P16, 40% of the income of the claimant has to be added towards future prospects which would result in the income to be Rs.17,500/- and the multiplier of '15' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.7,87,500/- (17,500 x 12 x 15 x 25%) towards 'loss of future income'.
9. The Tribunal has considered the laid up period as 3 months.
Since the claimant was hospitalized for two months, it would be appropriate to consider the laid up period as 5 months.
As a consequence, the amount of Rs.27,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would stand enhanced to Rs.62,500/- (12,500 X 5 months).

10. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant and he was hospitalized for 58 days, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,25,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.75,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,25,000/- towards loss of amenities, as against the sum of Rs.20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

12. Having regard to the length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital, the claimant would also be entitled to 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges' at Rs.50,000/- as against the sum of Rs.17,400/- awarded by the Tribunal.

13. The sums awarded as medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence,
does not call for modification and hence confirmed.
14.

Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

1. Pain and sufferings 1,25,000 2.
Loss of future income 7,87,500 3.
Medical expenses 21,825

Loss of income during the laid 62,500 4.
up period Conveyance, food, 50,000 5. nourishment, attendant charges 6.
Loss of amenities in life 1,25,000
Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.11,71,825/- as against Rs.4,40,444/-, along with interest from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
17. The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.
18. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
19. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
